annotations.title: Find lots that match a list

description: Find the lots in one live Bucky city that match a list. Pass `city` or `geoDivisionId` with `thesis` (plain words), `criteria` (square feet, dollars), or both; or pass a saved `profileId`. Returns countOutcome (exact, partial, at_least, estimate, or unavailable), screeningRunId, and selected lots ranked largest first with a pass, fail, or not_available verdict per filter. totalMatches is a compatibility value and can be returned-page size when the total is unavailable. Report a not_available filter; never present the count as filtered by it. The execution preserves selection for optional candidate assessment; assessment candidate counts are separate from search totals. Returns candidates, counted suggestions and savedMatches. Candidate/suggestion criteria use the same square-foot boundary as the input, including canonical registry values and strategies. Present these alternatives before asking to save. Pass the selected criteria with save=true only after explicit approval, without re-reading the thesis. For a height the user wants to build ("10 to 14 storeys"), use criteria.permitted_stories or permitted_height_m: the maximum the lot's zone allows. criteria.stories is the building standing on the lot. Each lot has `lotId` for saveLot, `address` for getFeasibilitySnapshot and `parcelExternalId` for saveToProject. Assembly lots carry the same ids. At most 25 lots per call (`limit`, default 10). `page` says which matches these are (offset, returned, total, truncated); when truncated, call screenLots with `page.next` for the next lots. Paging reads only: it saves nothing and uses no list quota. save=true saves the list (write scope, counts against the plan list limit) and returns a CSV link of every match; the CSV needs a saved list, so links.csv is null without one.

assembly.description: Assembly mode: also return candidate assemblies, 2 to maxLots adjacent lots that each pass criteria and together meet minCombinedAreaSqft and/or minCombinedFrontageFt. Use for "two or three adjacent lots that combine to 10,000 sf"; put per-lot limits in criteria and the combined size here, not in minAreaSqft.

maxLots.description: Most lots in one assembly, 2 to 5. Default 3.

minCombinedAreaSqft.description: Combined lot area the assembly must reach, in square feet.

minCombinedFrontageFt.description: Combined frontage the assembly must reach, in feet: the sum of derived lot widths, an estimate.

sameZone.description: same (default): every lot in one zone code. family: one zone family. any: zones may differ.

city.description: City as the user said it, e.g. "Laval" or "Bedford, MA". Omit when you pass geoDivisionId or profileId.

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

criteria.description: Structured criteria. A field set here replaces the same field read from thesis.

assessed_value_per_buildable.description: Assessed total value (land and buildings) divided by the buildable floor area (lot area x the zone’s cited maximum FSR), in currency per square metre of floor area, inclusive bounds ($150 per sq ft = 1,614.59 per m²). Lots without a cited FSR or a usable assessment never match.

branches.description: Alternative strategies; nested registry values stay in canonical units.

assessed_value_per_buildable.description: Assessed total value (land and buildings) divided by the buildable floor area (lot area x the zone’s cited maximum FSR), in currency per square metre of floor area, inclusive bounds ($150 per sq ft = 1,614.59 per m²). Lots without a cited FSR or a usable assessment never match.

building_use.description: What the lot is used for today, read from the assessor's use code: office, mixed_use, retail, hospitality, industrial, multifamily, two_to_four_family, single_family, institutional, civic, religious, parking, vacant_land, other. "Commercial buildings, not houses or churches" is { any_of: ["office", "mixed_use", "retail"] } or { none_of: ["single_family", "two_to_four_family", "religious", "civic"] }.

contamination_risk.description: true: a gas station or auto-service business (repair, body shop, car wash) is mapped on the lot. { is: false } excludes those lots. A risk flag from OpenStreetMap and city business licences, not a site investigation: it misses former and unmapped businesses.

dwelling_count.description: Dwellings on the lot, as the assessment roll states them (Montréal: nombre de logements). "A single-family house" is { min: 1, max: 1 }; "duplex or triplex" is { min: 2, max: 3 }. Lots whose roll states no count never match.

existing_coverage_pct.description: Building footprint area on the lot as a percentage of lot area, 0-100. An underbuilt screen is { max: 20 }. Footprints can be years old: check the city honesty note.

existing_use_class.description: What stands on the lot: place_of_worship (church, temple, mosque, synagogue…), fuel_station, auto_service (repair, body, car wash), auto_sales (car dealer), else vacant, surface_parking or built. "Vacant lots or surface parking" is { any_of: ["vacant", "surface_parking"] }; "gas stations" is { any_of: ["fuel_station"] }; "church sites" is { any_of: ["place_of_worship"] }. Vacant means no building over 20 m² in any footprint source and no assessed building worth over 20% of the land. Québec lots without footprints use the assessment roll land-use code (CUBF 9100 = vacant). A mapped business on the lot wins over the footprint class. Fuel and auto-service sites are a contamination risk flag, not a site investigation.

exterior_material.description: The assessor's primary exterior wall as a family: masonry, wood, siding, stucco, concrete, metal, glass, other. "Brick buildings" is { any_of: ["masonry"] }.

frequent_transit_distance.description: Metres from the lot line to the nearest frequent bus stop or rapid-transit station.

hydrant_distance.description: Metres from the lot line to the nearest fire hydrant.

improvement_land_ratio.description: Building (improvement) value divided by land value, assessed or appraised, as a ratio: 0.25 = the building is worth a quarter of the land. A teardown screen is { max: 0.25 }.

land_value_per_buildable.description: Assessed land value divided by the buildable floor area (lot area x the zone’s cited maximum FSR), in currency per square metre of floor area, inclusive bounds ($150 per sq ft = 1,614.59 per m²). Lots without a cited FSR, a land/improvement split or a usable assessment never match.

lot_depth.description: Metres. A frontage the city publishes, else the side of the lot outline's oriented bounding rectangle.

lot_width.description: Metres. A frontage the city publishes, else the side of the lot outline's oriented bounding rectangle.

ocp_above_zoning.description: true: the lot's plan designation (Official Community Plan, or future land use map) allows more housing than its current zone (both ranked 1 rural, 2 low density, 3 medium density, 4 high density or mixed-use centre): a rezoning candidate. { is: false } keeps lots where both are ranked and the plan is not higher. Lots with an unranked zone or designation, no zone, or no designation match neither. A planning signal: a rezoning consistent with the plan is more likely to be supported, but this is not a rezoning approval or the density zoning permits today.

owner_class.description: Owner class of the lot, from ParcelMap BC owner type or an open assessment roll: private, municipal, provincial (or state), federal, crown_agency (or public agency), public_other, institutional (religious, charitable, education, health), first_nations, mixed_ownership (as the source states), unclassified, and public (any of municipal, provincial, federal, crown_agency, public_other). Institutional and First Nations land is not public. A lot with parcels of several classes holds all of them, so none_of ["public"] also drops a lot that is partly public and any_of ["private"] keeps it. "Not public land" is { none_of: ["public"] }, which keeps lots whose owner class is unknown; any_of drops them. "Private" is the registered owner type, not a title search.

ownership_form.description: Ownership form: fee_simple (land title), strata_condo, co_op, leasehold, mixed. "Land title only" is { none_of: ["strata_condo", "co_op", "leasehold", "mixed"] }, which keeps lots whose form is unknown; any_of drops them.

parking_coverage.description: Mapped surface-parking area on the lot as a percentage of lot area, 0-100. Church parking lots: place_of_worship true with { min: 25 }. An office or store with a large parking field: existing_use_class built with { min: 50 }. 0 means the map shows no parking.

permitted_height_m.description: Metres. Maximum building height the lot may reach: the city's height overlay map where one sets it (Toronto), else the zone rules. { min: 30 } keeps lots allowed at least 30 m.

permitted_stories.description: Maximum storeys the lot's zone allows, from the zone rules. { min: 10 } keeps lots whose zone allows at least 10 storeys; "10 to 14 storey rental" is { min: 10, max: 14 }. Not the building standing on the lot: that is `stories`.

place_of_worship.description: true: a church, temple, mosque, synagogue or other place of worship is mapped on the lot (OpenStreetMap, city heritage registers). { is: false } excludes those lots. Same lots as existing_use_class place_of_worship.

planned_transit_distance.description: Metres from the lot line to the nearest station of a rapid transit line that is planned or under construction (not yet open; never counted as frequent transit).

register_status.description: Historic register status: individually_listed, contributing, non_contributing, in_district (inside a register district, building not yet mapped), not_listed. "On the register" is { any_of: ["individually_listed", "contributing"] }. Register status is a research lead, not tax-credit eligibility. The federal 20% credit needs a certified historic structure; building age alone qualifies for nothing (the 10% pre-1936 credit was repealed in 2017).

stories.description: Above-grade stories: the assessor count where recorded (half stories are decimals, 1.5), otherwise estimated from building height at 3 m per storey. "1-2 story" is { max: 2 }.

street.description: Street names as the lot address carries them, upper case with the suffix abbreviated: "STATE ST", "BANK ST". { any_of: [...] } keeps lots on those streets. Matches the lot's address, not every street it touches: a corner lot counts once.

subdivision_yield.description: Lot area divided by the zone's minimum lot area: how many minimum-size lots the parcel could hold by area. "Could be subdivided" is { min: 2 }; "into 3 lots" is { min: 3 }. Ignores frontage, streets and lot shape: a candidate, not a subdivision approval.

tax_exempt.description: true: the assessment roll classes the property as exempt from property tax (public, religious, charitable and similar owners). { is: false } keeps taxable lots only. Read from rolls that state both values; personal exemptions (senior, veteran) do not count.

titled_unit_count.description: Titled units on the parcel: 1 for a land-title lot, the strata unit count otherwise.

tract_rent_2br.description: CMHC Rental Market Survey average monthly rent for a 2-bedroom purpose-built rental unit in the census tract holding the lot centre, CAD, inclusive bounds. Lots in tracts CMHC does not publish never match.

tract_rental_vacancy.description: CMHC Rental Market Survey vacancy rate, all bedroom types, purpose-built rental, in the census tract holding the lot centre, percent (1.5 = 1.5%), inclusive bounds. Lots in tracts CMHC does not publish never match.

typology.description: Current site use from site_typologies, not what can be built. Exact typology IDs; sector-only lots do not match any_of. none_of keeps lots whose typology is unknown.

use_sector.description: Current site use from site_typologies, not what can be built. Sector IDs; includes sector-only assignments. none_of keeps lots whose sector is unknown.

year_built.description: Year the main building was built, inclusive bounds.

zone_family.description: The zone's dominant use: residential, mixed, commercial, industrial, public, recreation, agricultural, forest. "Zoned residential or mixed" is { any_of: ["residential", "mixed"] }. Québec zones read the zone letter (H, M, C, I, P/U, R, A, F); other zones a family classified from the zone name and purpose. The family names the dominant use; the bylaw still decides which uses are permitted.

lot_depth.description: Metres. A frontage the city publishes, else the side of the lot outline's oriented bounding rectangle.

lot_width.description: Metres. A frontage the city publishes, else the side of the lot outline's oriented bounding rectangle.

maxAssessed.description: Highest assessed total value, in dollars.

minAssessed.description: Lowest assessed total value, in dollars.

minHomes.description: Homes allowed, at least N. A zone-level estimate.

namedAreaIds.description: Submarket (named area) ids. Use `thesis` to match submarkets by name.

namedAreaKinds.description: Named-area kinds from the registry, e.g. ["downtown"]. Each resolves to this city's areas of that kind and is added to namedAreaIds, so no id lookup is needed. A city with no area of a kind is an error that names it ("no downtown area on file"); it never screens the whole city instead. Midtown and uptown are names, not kinds: use thesis.

ocp_above_zoning.description: true: the lot's plan designation (Official Community Plan, or future land use map) allows more housing than its current zone (both ranked 1 rural, 2 low density, 3 medium density, 4 high density or mixed-use centre): a rezoning candidate. { is: false } keeps lots where both are ranked and the plan is not higher. Lots with an unranked zone or designation, no zone, or no designation match neither. A planning signal: a rezoning consistent with the plan is more likely to be supported, but this is not a rezoning approval or the density zoning permits today.

overlayExcludeKinds.description: Overlay kinds a lot must not overlap. A lot passes only if it was evaluated for every excluded kind; an unevaluated kind is reported not_available.

overlayKinds.description: Overlay kinds a lot must overlap by at least 1 m². A kind the city has not evaluated is reported not_available, never applied.

owner_class.description: Owner class of the lot, from ParcelMap BC owner type or an open assessment roll: private, municipal, provincial (or state), federal, crown_agency (or public agency), public_other, institutional (religious, charitable, education, health), first_nations, mixed_ownership (as the source states), unclassified, and public (any of municipal, provincial, federal, crown_agency, public_other). "Not public land" is { none_of: ["public"] }, which keeps lots whose owner class is unknown; any_of drops them. "Private" is the registered owner type, not a title search.

ownership_form.description: Ownership form: fee_simple (land title), strata_condo, co_op, leasehold, mixed. "Land title only" is { none_of: ["strata_condo", "co_op", "leasehold", "mixed"] }, which keeps lots whose form is unknown; any_of drops them.

planned_transit_distance.description: Metres from the lot line to the nearest station of a rapid transit line that is planned or under construction (not yet open; never counted as frequent transit).

projectInputs.description: What the project is, checked against a use's structured conditions.

buildingForm.description: standalone, or unit_in_building (a unit inside a building with other occupants).

grossFloorAreaSqft.description: Gross floor area of the project, in square feet.

register_status.description: Historic register status: individually_listed, contributing, non_contributing, in_district (inside a register district, building not yet mapped), not_listed. "On the register" is { any_of: ["individually_listed", "contributing"] }. Register status is a research lead, not tax-credit eligibility. The federal 20% credit needs a certified historic structure; building age alone qualifies for nothing (the 10% pre-1936 credit was repealed in 2017).

stories.description: Above-grade stories: the assessor count where recorded (half stories are decimals, 1.5), otherwise estimated from building height at 3 m per storey. "1-2 story" is { max: 2 }.

street.description: Street names as the lot address carries them, upper case with the suffix abbreviated: "STATE ST", "BANK ST". { any_of: [...] } keeps lots on those streets. Matches the lot's address, not every street it touches: a corner lot counts once.

subdivision_yield.description: Lot area divided by the zone's minimum lot area: how many minimum-size lots the parcel could hold by area. "Could be subdivided" is { min: 2 }; "into 3 lots" is { min: 3 }. Ignores frontage, streets and lot shape: a candidate, not a subdivision approval.

tax_exempt.description: true: the assessment roll classes the property as exempt from property tax (public, religious, charitable and similar owners). { is: false } keeps taxable lots only. Read from rolls that state both values; personal exemptions (senior, veteran) do not count.

titled_unit_count.description: Titled units on the parcel: 1 for a land-title lot, the strata unit count otherwise.

tract_rent_2br.description: CMHC Rental Market Survey average monthly rent for a 2-bedroom purpose-built rental unit in the census tract holding the lot centre, CAD, inclusive bounds. Lots in tracts CMHC does not publish never match.

tract_rental_vacancy.description: CMHC Rental Market Survey vacancy rate, all bedroom types, purpose-built rental, in the census tract holding the lot centre, percent (1.5 = 1.5%), inclusive bounds. Lots in tracts CMHC does not publish never match.

typology.description: Current site use from site_typologies, not what can be built. Exact typology IDs; sector-only lots do not match any_of. none_of keeps lots whose typology is unknown.

usePermission.description: A specific use judged by its permission status per zone, from reviewed bylaw mappings. Matches as of right, and with conditions only when every condition passes projectInputs. Existing-only uses never match. A zone with no reviewed mapping is unknown: counted in usePermission.unknownLotCount, never matched, never called prohibited or needing rezoning. A broad-code match alone is a candidate, not permission.

notListedZoneFamilies.description: Opt in to rezoning candidates: zones of these families where the use is not listed. A candidate is an assessed opportunity, never a permission.

statuses.description: Statuses that count as a match. Default as_of_right and with_conditions; with_conditions matches only when every condition passes the project inputs. existing_only never matches.

useCodes.description: Use codes to screen for. A parent code (COMMERCIAL_ENTERTAINMENT) matches its children.

use_sector.description: Current site use from site_typologies, not what can be built. Sector IDs; includes sector-only assignments. none_of keeps lots whose sector is unknown.

year_built.description: Year the main building was built, inclusive bounds.

zoneCodes.description: Zone codes from the city's own vocabulary, e.g. RM-4.

zone_family.description: The zone's dominant use: residential, mixed, commercial, industrial, public, recreation, agricultural, forest. "Zoned residential or mixed" is { any_of: ["residential", "mixed"] }. Québec zones read the zone letter (H, M, C, I, P/U, R, A, F); other zones a family classified from the zone name and purpose. The family names the dominant use; the bylaw still decides which uses are permitted.

cursor.description: Next page of the same box. Copy page.next from the prior result: it carries the cursor with the box. Do not combine with thesis. Reads only; nothing is saved.

geoDivisionId.description: Division id, from an earlier screenLots or cityInventory result.

groupBy.description: Adds `groups`: every match split by one field, with lot count and summed area per group, the top groupLimit groups plus other / withheld / unknown buckets that add up to the match count. owner: largest owners; only corporations and public bodies are named, other owners are counted as "private owners (not named)". owner_type: corporation, government, trust, individual or unclassified. lot_size: area bands. year_built: decades. First page only.

groupLimit.description: Groups to list before the rest are summed as other. Default 10, at most 25.

groupOrder.description: lots (default): most matching lots first. area: largest summed lot area first. lot_size and year_built ignore groupOrder and groupLimit: they list every band in its own order.

hygiene.description: Default true. Ad-hoc lists leave out public owners (owner_class), cap lot size at 5 acres unless criteria set any lot-size minimum or maximum, and ignore assessed values under $100,000 where the city stores them, unless criteria set the same field. Each default is named in notes. false skips them. Ignored with profileId: a saved list runs as saved.

limit.description: Lots to return. Default 10, at most 25 per call; page.next reads the next lots. countOutcome states whether the total is exact, partial, at_least (a lower bound), estimate (about), or unavailable.

profileId.description: Saved list id. Runs the saved city and criteria. Do not combine with city, thesis, or criteria.

save.description: true saves the list to the account. Default false. Search execution history is recorded.

sort.description: Order of the returned lots across every match. Default lot_area_desc (largest first). land_value_per_buildable_asc / assessed_value_per_buildable_asc: lowest assessed land (or total) value per buildable sq ft first, for "cheapest land per buildable foot". Lots with no cited FSR or usable assessment come last.

thesis.description: The list in plain words, e.g. "industrial lots over half an acre outside the floodplain".

totals.description: true adds `totals`: the match count and summed lot area (sq ft and acres) of every match, not only the page. Use it for "how many acres" instead of adding up pages. groupBy implies it. First page only.
